verdict.rationale: Nitrokey's own docs list an "SSH Keys" page under the FIDO2 feature section, and the product page says it handles SSH login using certificates. The OpenPGP docs also list on-device key generation and touch confirmation, and PIV is a documented feature. The evidence is mostly headings, though, so it does not show an end-to-end setup where SSH server access actually requires a physical touch. Touch confirmation is documented only for OpenPGP and only on the Nitrokey 3. Missing for 10: detailed docs on FIDO2 sk-ssh key generation and touch enforcement, an explicit PIV-to-SSH workflow, confirmation that touch is required for each SSH authentication, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my SSH keys can be hardware-backed on the device — via FIDO2 sk-ssh keys, PIV, or OpenPGP — so server access requires a physical touch

citations.quote: Login to computers and network services (e.g. SSH) using certificates.
